q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) >= 5 ) A
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) >= 5 ) A
explanation: Q1 groups courses by CLASS and selects those with a count of at least 5, which means it considers the total number of courses in each class. Q2, on the other hand, groups courses by CLASS and then by STUDENT, ensuring that each student is counted only once per class, and it selects classes where the count of distinct students is at least 5.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when a class has 5 or more unique students, but the total number of courses in that class is less than 5.
